follow100Note: The pattern is the same as last quarter: the stock portfolio added $15.79 of every $100 — more than the $12.75 the operating businesses earned after tax. That is why Berkshire's headline profit swings with the market, and why Buffett tells investors to watch operating earnings instead. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: Berkshire has no single gross-profit line: costs are split following the 10-Q's own structure.

kpis.label: Operating earnings
kpis.note: +16% YoY — the number Buffett says matters

oneTimers: Investment gains are mostly paper gains. Of the $16.1B pre-tax investment gains, $10.9B was an increase in unrealized gains on stocks Berkshire still holds; realized gains on sales were $1.8B after tax. Next quarter the unrealized part can just as easily reverse.
A currency swing flatters 'Other' operating earnings: a $326M gain on Berkshire's non-U.S.-dollar debt this quarter versus an $877M loss a year ago.
No Kraft Heinz impairment this year. The $3.76B write-down sat in Q2 2025, which is part of why this quarter's year-ago comparison looks so strong.
otherDetail: Investment gains of $16,077M — mostly unrealized gains on Berkshire's stock portfolio — plus $248M of equity-method earnings, less $105M attributable to noncontrolling interests.

segments.name: Insurance premiums earned
segments.note: Premiums from GEICO, reinsurance and primary insurance. Barely grew — Berkshire is still turning away business it thinks is underpriced.

segments.note: The biggest bucket: everything the manufacturing, service and retailing businesses sell — from Dairy Queen to Precision Castparts to Pilot truck stops.

segments.note: What the insurance float and the cash pile earn — mostly interest on Treasury bills now, plus dividends. Down a touch as lower rates cut what the float earns.

segments.note: Berkshire Hathaway Energy: electric and gas utilities, pipelines, renewables.

segments.note: Smaller service income inside the railroad and energy group.

takeaways.text: Operating earnings rose 16% to $13.0B. Manufacturing, service and retailing jumped 24% to $4.5B, energy rose 27% and BNSF 6% — while insurance underwriting fell 13% and insurance investment income fell 9% as lower rates bit.
takeaways.title: Operating earnings did the quiet work

takeaways.text: Net earnings more than doubled to $25.7B from $12.4B, but $12.7B of that (after tax) is investment gains, mostly paper gains on the stock portfolio. A year ago the same line was far smaller and Kraft Heinz took a $3.8B write-down.
takeaways.title: Headline profit doubled — mostly the stock market

takeaways.text: Berkshire repurchased about $4.5B of its own stock in the quarter, after only about $0.3B in Q1 — bringing the six-month total to $4.8B. The insurance float grew to $177.5B.
takeaways.title: Buybacks woke up

verdict: Berkshire's operating earnings rose 16% to $13.0B as its manufacturing and retail businesses jumped — and $16.1B of investment gains, mostly paper gains on its stock portfolio, more than doubled headline profit to $25.7B.
